Senses.Explanation: This is a blow delivered immediately as the next move in a live exchange: “then struck” or “thereupon hit.” The ordinary sequence marker plus action becomes exceptionally dense public-interview narration, and the striker is not automatically the teaching master. Yangqi Fanghui strikes an unnamed monk repeatedly, but a different unnamed monk immediately strikes Yangqi back. Linji Yixuan strikes after a bow, after Luopu Yuanan shouts, and when asked about the true person of no rank. Mazu Daoyi strikes after a question about the coming from the west and adds that if he did not strike, all quarters would laugh at him. Huayan Shengke recounts receiving a punch from Jiuyuan, immediately striking him, and striking again when Jiuyuan hesitates. Dadian Baotong strikes an unnamed head monk and drives him out of the monastery. An unnamed monk deals one palm slap to the source-attested Zhuyuan master, who says that he brought it on himself. Nanyuan Huiyong's record places an immediate blow after the questioner's two shouts and Nanyuan's taking up the staff; a later comment by Xuedou Chongxian uses the parallel “then applied the staff” formula after raising Mazu's circle case. These are differences of actor, recipient, instrument, and consequence within one immediate-action construction, not different referents. The records state the acts and their consequences but do not assign every such blow one unstated purpose.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count: 7,585 occurrences in 360 texts; the framed master-action form occurs 4,254 times in 271 texts. Eleven curated occurrences distinguish exact striker from recipient, record owner, and later commenter. The two unnamed strikers remain anonymous only after the complete six-rung attribution ladder; all named masters use roster spelling where available, while Huayan Shengke and the place-titled Zhuyuan Heshang remain explicit non-roster reconciliation cases. Family checks cover “then shouted,” “then applied the staff,” staff, shout, bow, and the true person of no rank. Immediate sequence, explicit object, palm-slap complement, repetition, and expulsion remain one verbal construction rather than separate things.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師便打。僧擬提坐具。師又打云。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Yangqi Fanghui (楊岐方會和尚語錄), Yangqi Fanghui's examination exchange: Yangqi strikes the unnamed monk, the monk moves to raise his sitting cloth, and Yangqi strikes again. Yangqi is the striker and record owner; the monk is the recipient.

Occurrences.Kwic: 也是。僧便打。師云。老僧過在什麼處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Yangqi Fanghui (楊岐方會和尚語錄): an unnamed monk immediately strikes Yangqi Fanghui, and Yangqi asks where his own fault lies. All six attribution rungs, including parallel versions in Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters, leave the striking monk unnamed; Yangqi is the recipient and record owner, not the striker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臨濟見僧來舉起拂子僧禮拜師便打
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jade-Flower Collection from the Transmission of the Lamp, fragment (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), in a raised case explicitly beginning with Linji Yixuan's name: Linji raises the whisk, the unnamed monk bows, and Linji strikes. Linji is the striker; the monk is the recipient; the compiler and later raisers do not own the act.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是無位真人師便打云無位真人是什麼
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jade-Flower Collection from the Transmission of the Lamp, fragment (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), Linji Yixuan section: an unnamed monk asks about the true person of no rank; Linji strikes and asks what that person is. Linji is the striker and respondent, not the unnamed questioner or the lamp compiler.

Occurrences.Kwic: 落浦遂喝，師便打之。因德山見僧參愛趁打
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), Linji Yixuan section: Linji questions Luopu Yuanan, Luopu shouts, and Linji strikes Luopu. The following clause introduces a separate Deshan Xuanjian anecdote; Deshan is neither striker nor recipient in the stored headword turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問如何是西來意師便打乃云我若不打汝諸方笑我也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jade-Flower Collection from the Transmission of the Lamp, fragment (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), Mazu Daoyi section: an unnamed monk asks the meaning of the coming from the west; Mazu strikes and says that if he did not strike the monk, all quarters would laugh at him. Mazu is striker and respondent; the monk is questioner and recipient.

Occurrences.Kwic: 淵與老僧一拳，老僧便打，淵擬議，老僧又打。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huayan Shengke (華嚴聖可禪師語錄), Huayan Shengke's first-person New Year's hall account: Jiuyuan punches Huayan; Huayan immediately strikes Jiuyuan and strikes him again when he hesitates. Huayan is the striker and narrator; Jiuyuan is the first striker and then recipient. Huayan Shengke is source-attested but not yet rostered.

Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄), section headed Chan Master Dadian of Chaozhou: Dadian Baotong summons the unnamed head monk, confirms that he gave Han Yu the same response, then strikes the head monk and drives him out of the monastery. Dadian is the striker; the head monk is recipient; Han Yu is an earlier interlocutor, not an actor in the blow.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧便打一掌，師拓開云：山僧招得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of the Tiansheng Era (天聖廣燈錄), section headed Chan Master of Zhuyuan Mountain in Jingnan (荊南府竹園山禪師): an unnamed monk slaps Zhuyuan Heshang; Zhuyuan pushes him away and says that this mountain monk brought it on himself. All six rungs leave the striking monk unnamed. The source preserves the recipient only by place-title, so he is named here as Zhuyuan Heshang, source-attested but personally unplaceable.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師見僧來，劃一圓相云：入也打，不入也打。僧纔入，師便打。僧云：和尚打某甲不得。師靠却拄杖休去。雪竇云：二俱不了，和尚打某甲不得。靠却拄杖，擬議不來，劈脊便棒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Joint Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), Mazu Daoyi section: Mazu draws a circle and strikes the unnamed monk when he enters it. The same stored witness then marks Xuedou Chongxian's later comment, which ends with the family formula ‘then apply the staff.’ Mazu owns the headword blow; Xuedou owns only the later comment.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是第一句？師云：汝誠道看。僧便喝，師拍手云：大眾好喝。僧又喝，師拈棒，僧擬議，師便打。師上堂示眾云：諸方秖具啐啄同時句，不具啐啄同時用。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of the Tiansheng Era (天聖廣燈錄), section headed Nanyuan Huiyong of the Baoying Chan Cloister in Ruzhou: an unnamed monk shouts twice; Nanyuan applauds the first shout, takes up the staff after the second, and strikes when the monk hesitates. The following hall-address marker belongs to Nanyuan's next discourse. Nanyuan is striker and respondent; the monk is shouter and recipient.
